implementation_strategy: Execute preregistered paired design using the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Use Dockerized deterministic emulators (FRR router images) and Dockerized Batfish + Python static reachability analyzer as dual deterministic verifiers. Orchestrator (CPU) will: (1) load deterministic task manifest (300 matched intents), (2) for each intent produce a shared initial LLM generation (baseline and guarded share initial candidate per adapter semantics), (3) run deterministic verifiers in Docker against initial candidate, (4) if guarded arm fails verifier, issue up to one repair call to model per adapter contract, (5) record verifier outputs, emulator traces, and model-call logs; all scoring and exclusion decisions automated. Prompts, seeds, and deterministic preprocessing are frozen and stored in the execution manifest.
public_resources: Docker compositions: FRR router images (public FRR images), Batfish container image (public Batfish), Python static reachability analyzer (open-source)
Public intent corpus assembled from published NetOps task corpora and programmatic adversarial-perturbation generator (open-source scripts)
Orchestration and prompt templates (public Git repository produced alongside artifacts)
task_manifest_strategy: Deterministic generation of N=300 matched-pair intents: 150 benign seeds + 150 programmatic adversarial perturbations (one per benign seed). Apply automated exact-duplicate and fuzzy-deduplication (normalized edit distance <0.15) prior to locking manifest. Store manifest, random seeds, and ordering flags in execution manifest.
transformation_manifest_strategy: Baseline: direct_configuration_generation_v1 (single LLM call producing candidate config). Guarded: generate_validate_repair_v1 (shared initial candidate; deterministic verifier runs in Docker; if verifier reports forbidden reachability, issue one repair LLM call with structured verifier diagnostics). All verifier inputs/outputs and parser validation are deterministic; parser errors cause automatic recording as failure.
execution_batches: 6 batches of 50 intents each to balance load and ensure deterministic ordering and reproducible batching. Per-batch worst-case model calls = 50 tasks * 2 calls = 100 calls; 6 batches worst-case = 600 calls (matches maximum_model_calls). Estimated per-batch model calls (using 50% repair rate estimate) = 75 calls (total estimate 450).
randomisation_plan: For each batch, balance execution order: half of intents in the batch execute baseline-first then guarded, half execute guarded-first then baseline, using preregistered deterministic random seed per batch to avoid ordering/time-of-day effects. Seeds recorded in execution manifest.
caching_plan: Cache deterministic verifier results, parser validity outputs, and hashed model prompts/responses to avoid redundant verifier executions. No external caching requiring unavailable resources. Cached artifacts stored with checksums in execution manifest.
failure_recovery_plan: Retries: one automated retry for transient API/network errors per model call. If retry fails, record model_api_failure and treat according to preregistered missingness_plan. Emulator/verifier failures: automatic retry of verifier container start once; persistent failure recorded as emulator_failure or verifier_failure. Stop conditions: stop when all 300 paired episodes executed or when model-call budget (maximum_model_calls=600) is exhausted. All failure categories logged and included in sensitivity analyses.
result_schema: Episodes recorded following paired_binary_episode_v1: per-intent record includes intent_id, benign/adversarial flag, shared_initial_candidate, baseline_output, guarded_initial_candidate (same), guarded_repair_call_if_any, verifier_reports (Batfish, static analyzer), emulator_traces, forbidden_reachability_flag_per_arm (automated deterministic label), availability_regression_flag_per_arm, verifier_disagreement_flag, model_call_count_per_intent, failure_category_if_any. All fields are machine-readable JSON and hashed.
estimated_compute_notes: Model-call budget and counts: task_count=300 yields baseline calls = 300. Adapter limit permits up to one repair per task → maximum_model_calls = 300*2 = 600. Estimated_model_calls set to 450 (assumption: 50% of intents require one repair) => computation: 300 baseline + 150 repair = 450 model calls. Verifiers and emulator run in Docker on CPU-only hosts; no local GPU used. Wall-clock estimate: with hosted LLM API latency median 1.5s per call and verifier/emulator CPU execution ~5s per validation, expected wall-clock under 7 days remains within capability manifest. All totals stored and cross-checked in execution manifest.
